heading: Hollywood special ambassador (2025)
body: On January 16, 2025, President-elect Donald Trump named Gibson, alongside Sylvester Stallone and Jon Voight, as one of three [[hollywood-special-ambassadors|Hollywood special ambassadors]] who would serve as his "eyes and ears" in the entertainment capital.[n] The appointment surprised Gibson himself; in a statement distributed hours later by his publicist he said, "I got the tweet at the same time as all of you and was just as surprised. Nevertheless, I heed the call."[n] He added, "Any chance the position comes with an Ambassador's residence?" — a reference to the destruction of his Malibu, California home in the recent California wildfires.[n]

heading: Hollywood special ambassador (2025)
body: On January 16, 2025, President-elect Donald Trump announced in a social media post that Stallone, along with Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, would serve as one of three [[hollywood-special-ambassadors|Hollywood special ambassadors]] acting as his "eyes and ears" in the entertainment capital.[n] Trump framed the goal as "bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK — BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!", a reference widely read as addressing runaway production driven by foreign tax incentives in Britain, Hungary, Australia and Canada.[n]

heading: Hollywood special ambassador (2025)
body: Voight was named on January 16, 2025 by President-elect Donald Trump as one of three [[hollywood-special-ambassadors|Hollywood special ambassadors]], together with Mel Gibson and Sylvester Stallone, tasked with being Trump's "eyes and ears" in the entertainment capital.[n] The initiative was aimed at reversing the loss of film and television business to foreign countries offering studios generous tax incentives.[n]

heading: Darrin Bell arrest (2025)
body: In January 2025 the paper drew attention when [[darrin-bell|Darrin Bell]], a Pulitzer Prize-winning cartoonist known for his work with The Washington Post, was arrested in Sacramento County, California on felony child pornography charges.[n] Bell was booked on January 15, 2025 following an investigation by Sacramento Valley Internet Crimes Against Children detectives that reportedly began with a tip about 18 files of child sexual abuse material and ultimately linked 134 videos to an account allegedly controlled by Bell.[n] Badlands Media commentary highlighted the irony that Bell had won a Pulitzer for work aimed at critics of child grooming.[n]
